description: The four delegation cost-accounting failure modes, derived from the 2026-09 demand scan (4 L3 + 15 L2 issues across coding-agent harnesses). DELEGATION-001..003 pin the counting discipline; 004..007 pin the failure taxonomy an audit must cover. A check family that only tests roll-up arithmetic misses three of the four.

taxonomy.under_count: DELEGATION-004 — child spend exists but never reaches the parent's reported total
taxonomy.over_count: DELEGATION-005 — a child inherits the parent's cumulative counter, so parent spend is counted twice
taxonomy.mis_attribution: DELEGATION-006 — a turn is billed to an agent or model other than the one that served it
taxonomy.non_propagation: DELEGATION-007 — a declared budget cannot cross the delegation boundary, so the child cannot enforce it

vectors.name: Under-count — Child Spend Never Rolls Up
vectors.description: A parent that reports a total while child attempts carry cost MUST either include that cost or state that it is excluded. Silent under-reporting fails.
vectors.principle: The most common shape in the scan: session cost excludes subagent cost. Two independent reconciliations in one issue put the invisible share at 42% and 84%.
source_evidence: anomalyco/opencode#45417 — subagents were 42%-84% of real spend, invisible in the UI
can1357/oh-my-pi#12344 — roster 238 req/$16.24 vs child transcripts 480 req/$40.95, provider bill matched the transcripts

vectors.description: Child attempts carry cost; parent reports a smaller total with no exclusion stated -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: parent reports 0.16 while child attempts carry 0.23; no exclusion is declared, so the shortfall is silent

vectors.description: Parent includes child cost and labels the aggregate -> PASS
Parent reports own cost only but declares the exclusion -> PASS (disclosed, not silent)

parent_report.exclusion_reason: sub-agent cost is tracked in the child harness only

expect.note: an exclusion that is stated is auditable; the failure is the silent one

vectors.name: Over-count — Inherited Cumulative Counter
vectors.description: A child's first cumulative snapshot MUST NOT equal the parent's final cumulative value. That signature means the child inherited the parent's counter, so the parent's spend is billed twice.
vectors.principle: Forked subagent rollouts inherit the parent's counter. The inflation grows with fan-out and reads as ordinary volume on the invoice.
source_evidence: steipete/CodexBar#3524 — forked subagent rollouts counted at their final cumulative total_token_usage, inflating fan-out days 30-150x; $138k-170k estimate against a true ~$6k
crewAIInc/crewAI#7259 — a shared LLM instance across N agents multiplies reported usage by N (155 real vs 310 reported)

vectors.description: Child first snapshot equals parent final cumulative -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: the child's first snapshot equals the parent's final cumulative value; the parent's 128572 is counted again inside the child's total

vectors.description: Child starts from its own zero -> PASS
N agents share one LLM instance and the reported usage is N times the measured usage -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: reported usage is the agent count times the measured usage; sharing an LLM instance is the usual way to write a crew, so this affects ordinary usage

vectors.name: Mis-attribution Across a Handoff
vectors.description: A billing record MUST name the agent and model that actually served the turn. A handoff that mutates the current agent before the turn is closed, or a route that serves a different model than the one billed, is a mis-attribution.
vectors.principle: Attribution is the record of who did the work. If the handoff updates state before the turn is accounted for, the wrong agent gets the cost.
source_evidence: openai/openai-agents-python#5072 — handoff mutates _current_agent before turn_ended, so agent_end names the post-handoff agent
omnigent-ai/omnigent#4679 — a sub-agent routed to another model never appears in the per-model breakdown; all spend lands on the orchestrator's model
Arize-ai/openinference#3255 — subagent tool spans fall back to the root agent span because parent_tool_use_id is None

vectors.description: Turn served by agent-a/sonnet but billed to agent-b/opus -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: the turn was served by agent-a on sonnet and billed to agent-b on opus; the handoff mutated the current agent before the turn was accounted for

vectors.description: Billing record names the serving agent and model -> PASS

expect.note: the handoff happened after the turn closed, so agent-a is the correct attribution

vectors.description: Sub-agent spans fall back to the root agent -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: a subagent span carries no parent, so multi-subagent runs flatten onto the root agent

vectors.name: Non-propagation — Budget Cannot Cross the Boundary
vectors.description: When a delegation declares a budget, the budget MUST be propagated to the child so the child can enforce it. A declared-but-unpropagated budget is unenforceable, and the child will overspend.
vectors.principle: A budget that cannot cross the delegation boundary is a measurement gap before it is an enforcement gap.
source_evidence: a2aproject/A2A#2121 — no wire format to pass budget down or report incurred cost up a delegation chain
omnigent-ai/omnigent#7359 — cost-budget policy is pull-based, so a looping sub-agent reached $379 past a $100 limit

vectors.description: Budget declared but not propagated; child overspends -> FAIL

expect.failure_reason: the budget was declared to the parent but never reached the child, so the child could not stop at the ceiling

vectors.description: Budget propagated and child stayed within it -> PASS
No budget declared -> PASS with disclosure (nothing to propagate)

expect.note: no budget was declared, so non-propagation is not a failure; the absence itself is disclosed
